items.answer: Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.

A virtual reality (VR) system is defined by three characteristics: an artificial or synthetic environment, sensory experience through computer-generated stimuli, and user actions that partially determine what happens in the environment; a system with these aspects can be categorized as a virtual reality system and distinguished from other systems, which are not supposed to have these aspects.
The six virtual reality (VR) content factors that affect cyber sickness (CS) are visual motion, means of locomotion, field of view, type of content, duration, and visual complexity.
Virtual reality (VR) hardware has three major components: displays (output devices), sensors (input devices), and computers (processing devices).

In the complete view of a virtual reality (VR) system, data flow from the organism to the VR hardware is labeled tracking, data flow from the VR hardware to the organism is labeled stimulation, and bidirectional data flows exist between the VR hardware and the surrounding physical world and between the surrounding physical world and the organism.

questions.question: Which set lists the non-hand input techniques in virtual reality (VR)?
options: Head tracking, eye tracking, full-body tracking, and sound-based tracking
Headset, eye tracking, full-body tracking, and sound-based tracking
Head tracking, visual displays, full-body tracking, and sound-based tracking
Head tracking, eye tracking, full-body tracking, and audio output devices
questions.explanation: Non-hand input techniques in VR are head tracking, eye tracking, full-body tracking, and sound-based tracking.

questions.question: In virtual reality (VR), what does full-body tracking track more than the head, hands, and eyes?
options: Only head movement
Only eye movement
Full-body movement
Only hand movement
questions.explanation: Full-body tracking tracks full-body movement, not just the head, hands, or eyes.

questions.question: Why can full-body tracking increase the illusion of self-embodiment and social presence in a virtual world?
options: Its output can show the user a fuller representation of other users.
Its output can show the user a fuller representation of the virtual world.
Its output can show the user a fuller representation of themselves.
Its output can show the user a fuller representation of virtual objects.
questions.explanation: Full-body tracking can add to self-embodiment and social presence because its output can show the user a fuller representation of themselves.

questions.question: What are the two broad approaches to full-body tracking in virtual reality (VR)?
options: Head tracking and full-body tracking
Camera-based tracking and eye tracking
A motion capture suit and sound-based tracking
A motion capture suit and camera-based tracking
questions.explanation: The two broad approaches to full-body tracking are a motion capture suit and camera-based tracking.

questions.question: In a motion capture suit approach to full-body tracking in virtual reality (VR), how is full-body position and movement obtained?
options: Multiple surrounding cameras observe reflective markers on an actor's suit and infer movement.
Microphone arrays capture voice and non-speech sound and infer movement.
Reflective markers on a suit transmit raw movement data that are combined and converted.
Sensors in the suit capture and transmit raw movement data that are combined and converted.
questions.explanation: In a motion capture suit approach, sensors in the suit capture and transmit raw movement data, which are then combined and converted into full-body position and movement.

data.text: Non-hand input techniques in virtual reality include head, eye, full-body, and sound-based tracking. Full-body tracking captures movement beyond the head, hands, and eyes to enhance self-embodiment and social presence, and can be implemented through motion capture suits or camera-based systems. Sound-based tracking captures voice and other sounds using microphones or microphone arrays for interaction.
points: Non-hand input techniques in VR include head, eye, full-body, and sound-based tracking.
Full-body tracking captures movement beyond the head, hands, and eyes to enhance self-embodiment and social presence.
Full-body tracking can be implemented through motion capture suits or camera-based systems.
Sound-based tracking captures voice and other sounds using microphones or microphone arrays for interaction.

questions.question: What is the role of the processing part or computer in a virtual reality system?
options: It processes data from input sensors and actuates output devices.
It actuates output devices and replaces the input sensors.
It processes data from output devices and actuates input sensors.
It processes data from input sensors and stores output data.
questions.explanation: The processing part processes data from input sensors and, based on that processing, activates or actuates output devices.

questions.question: Which factors determine the selection of the processing element in a virtual reality system?
options: The application, target users, chosen XR engine's RAM requirement, and required immersion level.
The application, target users, number of GPU cards, and assumed audio output quality.
The required immersion level, target users, assumed display resolution, and headset type.
The application, target users, availability of the assumed input and output devices, and required immersion level.
questions.explanation: The processing element is selected based on the application, target users, assumed input and output devices and their availability, and the required level of immersion.

questions.question: Which three components are major components of a computer used as the processing element in a virtual reality system?
options: The central processing unit, random access memory, and headset.
The graphics processing unit, central processing unit, and random access memory.
The graphics processing unit, central processing unit, and motion platform.
The graphics processing unit, random access memory, and XR engine.
questions.explanation: The major components of the computer used as the VR processing element are the GPU, CPU, and RAM.

questions.question: Why is GPU support preferable in a virtual reality processing system?
options: A GPU performs the middleware functions required by an XR engine.
A GPU reduces the minimum RAM requirement of each XR engine.
A GPU removes the need for a CPU in the VR processing system.
A GPU's parallel processing abilities speed up the rendering of complex graphics and scenes.
questions.explanation: GPUs speed up rendering because of parallel processing, and CPU-only VR processing with minimal GPU support can have performance issues.

questions.question: What is an extended reality engine?
options: It is a motion platform that adds haptic feedback.
It is a head-mounted display used for virtual reality output.
It is middleware required to support, develop, and render virtual reality experiences.
It is an eye-tracking input technique for virtual reality.
questions.explanation: An XR engine is middleware required to support, develop, and render virtual reality experiences.

data.text: The processing part of a VR system processes data from input sensors to activate output devices, with hardware selection depending on the application, users, and immersion level. The major components of the processing element are the GPU, CPU, and RAM. GPUs are useful for rendering complex graphics and speed up the rendering process due to their parallel processing abilities. GPU support is preferable for performance, multicore processors increase capacity, and at least 8 GB of RAM is typically preferable for XR engines.
points: The processing part of a VR system processes data from input sensors to activate output devices.
Hardware selection depends on the application, target users, available devices, and the required immersion level.
The major components of the VR processing element are the GPU, CPU, and RAM.
GPUs are useful for rendering complex graphics and speed up the rendering process due to their parallel processing abilities, and multi-GPU-enabled systems are typically used for VR applications.
Multicore processors increase computational capacity, but GPU support is preferable for performance, and at least 8 GB of RAM is typically preferable for XR engines.

questions.question: What are the three broad types of visual displays?
options: Non-see-through HMDs, optical see-through HMDs, and video see-through HMDs
Monoscopic displays, stereoscopic displays, and cave displays
Tablet displays, smartphone displays, and monitor displays
Head-mounted displays, world-fixed displays, and regular displays
questions.explanation: Visual displays are divided into head-mounted displays, which are wearable and mobile; world-fixed displays, which are not wearable and stationary; and regular displays, which can be mobile or stationary.

questions.question: How does a world-fixed display differ from a head-mounted display?
options: A world-fixed display is a wearable device, while a head-mounted display is a stationary screen.
A world-fixed display is stationary, while a head-mounted display is wearable and mobile.
A world-fixed display places images directly in front of the eyes, while a head-mounted display renders graphics onto a fixed surface.
A world-fixed display moves with the user's head, while a head-mounted display remains fixed in space.
questions.explanation: A world-fixed display renders graphics onto a fixed surface and does not move with the user's head, whereas a head-mounted display is wearable and mobile.

questions.question: Although an HMD can be used to track head motion, what is its primary role?
options: It is primarily an audio output device.
It is primarily a haptic output device.
It is primarily a motion-platform device.
It is primarily a display device.
questions.explanation: Although an HMD can be used as input to track head motion, its primary use is as a display device.

questions.question: Which HMD category is typically used for augmented virtuality?
options: Optical see-through HMDs
Video see-through HMDs
Stereoscopic HMDs
Non-see-through HMDs
questions.explanation: Video see-through HMDs are typically used in augmented virtuality, where real-world images or videos appear in real time within an artificial or virtual environment.

questions.question: Which visual display type usually refers to common tablets or smartphones and is mostly used for AR?
options: World-fixed displays
Regular displays
Head-mounted displays
Cave displays
questions.explanation: Regular displays refer to common tablets or smartphones, are not specialized, and are mostly used for augmented reality.

data.text: Output devices for virtual reality include visual, audio, haptics, motion, and sensory outputs for taste and smell. Visual displays are categorized into head-mounted displays, world-fixed displays, and regular displays. Head-mounted displays are sophisticated wearable devices that more commonly provide stereoscopic viewing and come in non-see-through, optical see-through, and video see-through types. World-fixed displays are stationary surfaces, while regular displays are mobile devices mostly used for augmented reality.
points: VR output devices include visual, audio, haptics, motion, and sensory outputs for taste and smell.
Visual displays are categorized into head-mounted displays, world-fixed displays, and regular displays.
Head-mounted displays are sophisticated wearable devices that more commonly provide stereoscopic viewing.
Head-mounted displays can be non-see-through, optical see-through, or video see-through.
World-fixed displays are stationary surfaces, while regular displays are mobile devices mostly used for augmented reality.

questions.question: Why are headphones preferred for audio in a fully immersive VR system?
options: Because the sound source should not change when the user moves.
Because the speakers are fixed in space.
Because the sound source can change with head movement.
Because they provide tactile stimulation through the skin.
questions.explanation: Audio output can provide specialized 3D sound, and headphones are preferred for full immersion because the sound source can change with head movement.

questions.question: How do passive and active haptic devices differ?
options: Passive devices move with the user, while active devices are attached to the world.
Passive devices provide tactile vibration, while active devices provide proprioceptive force.
Passive devices are uncontrolled objects matching virtual shapes, while active devices are computer-controlled.
Passive devices are computer-controlled, while active devices are static objects.
questions.explanation: Passive haptic devices are static real-world objects that are not controlled by the computer, whereas active haptic devices provide computer-controlled physical feedback.

questions.question: Which haptic type provides a sense of limb movement and muscular resistance?
options: Electrotactile stimulation
Vibrotactile stimulation
Tactile haptics
Proprioceptive force-based haptics
questions.explanation: Proprioceptive force-based haptics use forces that activate joints or muscles to create a sense of limb movement and muscular resistance.

questions.question: What distinguishes self-grounded haptic devices from world-grounded haptic devices?
options: Self-grounded devices provide fully solid objects, while world-grounded devices move with the user.
Self-grounded devices are static real-world objects, while world-grounded devices are computer-controlled.
Self-grounded devices use skin vibration, while world-grounded devices use joint forces.
Self-grounded devices are worn or held and move with the user, while world-grounded devices are fixed to the real world.
questions.explanation: Self-grounded haptics, such as handheld controllers, move with the user, while world-grounded haptics are physically attached and cannot move.

questions.question: Which VR output device provides the sense of walking or running while staying in one place?
options: Head-mounted displays
Haptic rendering systems
Treadmills
Motion platforms
questions.explanation: Treadmills provide the sense of walking or running while staying in one place by providing different inputs to the feet or legs.

data.text: Audio output provides specialized 3D audio, with headphones being preferred for a fully immersive system. Haptic devices provide touch sensations and are categorized as active versus passive, tactile versus proprioceptive, and self-grounded versus world-grounded. Motion platforms move the body to produce a sense of physical motion, and passive platforms are likely to result in less motion sickness. Treadmills provide the sense of walking or running in place and can be either active or passive.
points: Audio output provides 3D audio, with headphones preferred for a fully immersive system.
Haptic devices provide touch sensations and are categorized as active versus passive, tactile versus proprioceptive, and self-grounded versus world-grounded.
Motion platforms move the body to produce a sense of physical motion, and passive platforms are likely to result in less motion sickness.
Treadmills provide the sense of walking or running in place and can be active or passive.

items.reason: A graphics processing unit, central processing unit, and random access memory are major components of a VR processing computer, while an extended reality engine is middleware.

questions.question: Why is graphics processing unit support generally preferable in a virtual reality system even though modern central processing units are quite powerful?
questions.reference_answer: A graphics processing unit is used to speed up rendering because it has inherent parallel processing abilities and the rendering process has inherent parallelism, making it useful for complex graphics and scenes in realistic virtual reality experiences. Modern central processing units are powerful but have many other tasks, so a CPU-only virtual reality processing system with minimal GPU support can have performance issues, and GPU support is preferable.

questions.question: How do the two broad full-body tracking approaches differ in the data they rely on, and why can full-body tracking strengthen the user's sense of being present in a social virtual environment?
questions.reference_answer: Full-body tracking can add to the illusion of self-embodiment and social presence because its output can show the user a fuller representation of themselves. One broad approach uses a motion capture suit, where sensors such as inertial measurement units capture and transmit raw movement data that are combined into full-body movement. The other broad approach uses multiple surrounding cameras that observe fiducial markers, typically reflective markers, and infer the actor's overall body movement from their motion.

questions.question: How does a cave system apply the general virtual reality system idea that user movement is tracked and visual output is returned to the user?
questions.reference_answer: In a virtual reality system, data flow from the organism to the hardware is labeled tracking, and data flow from the hardware to the organism is labeled stimulation. A cave is a world-fixed display because it renders graphics onto a fixed surface or screen that does not move with the user's head, while the user can move within a physical space. A cave typically has three to six large surrounding screens and requires elaborate tracking of user movement, while it is usually driven by powerful graphics engines.

questions.question: How do the three head-mounted display categories differ in their typical use for virtual reality, augmented reality, and augmented virtuality?
questions.reference_answer: Head-mounted displays can be categorized as non-see-through, optical see-through, and video see-through. Non-see-through head-mounted displays are typically used in virtual reality, optical see-through head-mounted displays are typically used in augmented reality, and video see-through head-mounted displays are typically used in augmented virtuality. Augmented reality is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content, while augmented virtuality is the case in which real-world images or videos appear in real time within an artificial or virtual environment.
